sentences.l2: 二战期间，军方希望为轰炸机加装装甲，却不能把整架飞机都包住，否则机身太重，飞不远。
sentences.l1: During the Second World War, the military wanted to add armor to bombers, but could not cover the whole aircraft, or the fuselage would be too heavy and the plane could not fly far.

sentences.l2: 工程人员统计了返航飞机上的弹孔，发现机翼和机尾的弹孔最密集，发动机和驾驶舱附近却寥寥无几，于是有人主张加固弹孔多的部位。
sentences.l1: Engineers counted the bullet holes on returning aircraft and found that the holes were densest on the wings and tail, while there were very few near the engines and cockpit, so some people advocated reinforcing the parts with many bullet holes.

sentences.l2: 然而，一位统计学家提出了相反的看法：这些数据只来自成功返航的飞机，而被击中要害、没能飞回来的飞机根本没有进入统计。
sentences.l1: However, a statistician put forward the opposite view: this data came only from aircraft that had successfully returned, while aircraft that were hit in a vital spot and could not fly back had not entered the statistics at all.

sentences.l2: 换言之，发动机附近之所以弹孔少，并非因为那里不容易中弹，而是因为中弹的飞机大多坠毁了。
sentences.l1: In other words, the reason there are few bullet holes near the engines is not that those spots are hard to hit, but that most aircraft hit there crashed.

sentences.l2: 这种因样本选择不当而得出片面结论的现象，被称为幸存者偏差。
sentences.l1: This phenomenon of reaching one-sided conclusions because of improper sample selection is called survivorship bias.

sentences.l2: 它属于一种常见的逻辑谬误，会让我们在归因时只盯着看得见的成功者，而忽视沉默的失败者。
sentences.l1: It is a common logical fallacy, which makes us, when attributing causes, look only at the visible successful ones while ignoring the silent failures.
